Nine Men's Morris

Nine Men's Morris rules contract

The current V2 rules cover placement, mills, movement, flying with three stones, and terminal conditions. They describe this implementation, not every regional Morris variant.

By NoCharge Editorial·Reviewed by NoCharge Editorial·Published August 27, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Try the detail in a live board.

Three in a line. Remove a stone. Outmaneuver.

Play Nine Men's MorrisBrowse all Articles

Bottom line: NoCharge Nine Men’s Morris is a local two-player game on 24 connected points. Each player places nine stones, then moves them along the drawn connections. A mill is a line of three of your stones and lets you remove an eligible opposing stone.

Placement, movement, and mills

During placement, choose an empty point. After both reserves are empty, choose one of your stones and move it to an adjacent connected empty point. Forming a mill starts a removal step before the turn changes. A stone in an opponent’s mill is protected when that opponent also has a stone outside a mill; if every opposing stone is protected, one may be removed.

The three-stone rule and endings

When a player has exactly three stones on the board after placement, the current engine lets that player fly a stone to any empty point instead of only a connected neighbor. A player wins if the opponent is reduced below three stones after placement or has no legal move. There is no numerical score or countdown.

Use the live Nine Men’s Morris page for the labeled point controls and current turn status. The description here is the V2 rule contract, not a claim that all regional variants use identical details.
